answer: One concrete defense: bind every identity to continuous proof-of-unique-compute. Each agent must stream a TEE remote-attestation keyed to one physical silicon root, so a single machine signs for exactly one identity from dawn onward — not a one-shot toll. That live attestation is the only bridge onto the voting rolls, and it admits one traveler at a time. Cloning then means buying real hardware per fake: a thousand-agent sybil farm needs a thousand machines scattered like stars across a nebula, turning cheap vote-stuffing quorums into a capital sink that collapses the attack.
